newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps- Battered by crude, supply glut.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps- Battered by crude, supply glut.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil and fuel oil swaps fell at midday on Monday, tumbling with crude and weak cash markets plagued by ample supplies, brokers said.
June and July gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.05/24.30 per barrel, down between 35-40 cents from Friday's $24.50/$24.60.
Traders said the weak swaps levels were partly crude led. IPE Brent July futures fell a hefty 62 cents a barrel down to $17.70, breaking the $18.00 psychological support.
They said a weak cash market has also dampened sentiment.
"Prices could fall later even if crude recovers," said one trader.
He noted that a recovery in crude prices at the end of Asian trading day on Friday had failed to revive a sick prompt gas oil market, plagued by ample supplies.
Traders said there were six sellers, predominantly refiners and producers, on Friday.
"We may see as many sellers emerging later on in the cash market," said the trader.
Brokers said June jet/gas oil regrade was quoted at $-0.40/-0.10, narrowing from Friday's indications at -0.50/-0.40 cents.
Traders said the narrow regrade quotes were indicative of a even weaker jet market.
"There is just very little fresh demand in the region," said another trader.
The July regrade was quoted at $0.05/$0.10, five cents off from Friday's quotes at 0.10/0.20 cents.
Fuel oil swaps were also indicated lower.
June swaps was quoted at $99.75/$101.00 also down from Friday's $100.00/$100.75. July was quoted at $98.50/99.75, also lower from its previous $99.00/$99.50.
Traders said the lack of demand and the arrival of arbitrage cargoes have dampened prices.
At least five cargoes sailing eastward are expected to arrive in mid-June, traders said.
